question: A 47-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of gradually worsening facial and lower extremity swelling. She has had a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight gain during this time. Her blood pressure is 150/88 mm Hg. Examination shows periorbital edema and 2+ pretibial edema bilaterally. A 24-hour collection of urine shows 4.0 g of proteinuria. Microscopic examination of a kidney biopsy specimen shows thickening of the glomerular basement membrane. Electron microscopy shows dense subepithelial deposits. Further evaluation is most likely to show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Facial and lower extremity swelling" -> "Weight gain" -> "Hypertension" -> "Proteinuria" -> "Glomerular basement membrane thickening" -> "Dense subepithelial deposits on electron microscopy" -> "Anti-phospholipase A2 receptor antibodies" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Facial and lower extremity swelling" -> "Weight gain" -> "Hypertension" -> "Proteinuria" -> "Glomerular basement membrane thickening" -> "Dense subepithelial deposits on electron microscopy" -> "Anti-collagen type IV antibodies" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of facial and lower extremity swelling, weight gain, hypertension, proteinuria, glomerular basement membrane thickening, and dense subepithelial deposits on electron microscopy is most likely indicative of membranous nephropathy. Further evaluation is most likely to show anti-phospholipase A2 receptor antibodies rather than anti-collagen type IV antibodies.
